Abstract: A Pd-catalyzed highly selective tandem reaction of allenynes, aryl or alkenyl iodides, and sodium
azide for the synthesis of bicyclic 1,2,3-triazole derivatives with a very broad substrate scope including mono-
substituted, 1,3-disubstituted, and trisubstituted allenynes as well as dif ferent types of organic iodides has been
reported. Control experiments showed that the reaction went through a cascade allene difunctionalization/
W instein allylic azide rearrangement/intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloaddition process.
Keywords: Palladium; Bicyclic 1,2,3-triazole; Allylic azide rearrangement; Intramolecular cycloaddition
Intr oduction
Bicyclic 1,2,3-triazole derivatives are an important
class of nitrogen-containing heterocycles because of
their extensive applications in medicinal chemistry
(Figure 1).
[1]
T raditional approaches for bicyclic
triazole derivatives mainly rely on the intramolecular
[3 + 2]-cycloaddition of azide with alkyne.
[2–5]
Nowadays, the palladium-catalyzed intramolecular
coupling cyclizations of allenes bearing nucleophilic
functionalities with aryl iodides has been a powerful
way to construct carbocyclic or heterocyclic
compounds.
[6–12]
However , very limited reports have
been disclosed for the intermolecular reaction of
allenes, aryl iodides and nucleophiles,
[13,14]
due to the
challenge to control the regio- and stereo-selectivity .
W e envisioned that if the 1,5-allenyne was applied
instead of the simple allene with or ganic halides and
sodium azide, a mixture of allylicazide isomers Z- or
E-Int-1 and Int-2 would also be produced.
[15,16]
After a
Cu-catalyzed intramolecular azide-alkyne
cycloaddition,
[2–5]
bicyclic 1,2,3-triazole products P-1
with an eight-membered ring and P-2 with a six-
membered ring may be obtained from Z-Int-1 and Int-
2, respectively , with E-Int-1 remaining. Here the
challenge would be the control of selectivity for the
exclusive formation for one of the three products P-1,
P-2, and E-Int-1. Here we wish to report the highly
selective formation of [4.3.0]-bicyclic products P-2 via
the mixed intermediacy of all three intermediates, Z- or
E-Int-1 and Int-2 (Scheme 1).

T o gain insights into the mechanism, a series of
control experiments were performed. When the reac-
tion of 1 a with iodobenzene in the presence of NaN
3
was conducted at room temperature, surprisingly , three
allyl azides 3 aa, Z-4 aa, and E-4 aa were obtained in
the NMR yield of 17%, 44%, and 34%, respectively
(Scheme 3). It was observed that these three isomers
may interconvert after being stirred in DMAc at room
temperature for 43 hours (Eqs. 1–3, Scheme 3).
[21]
In
addition, heating the mixtures of allylicazide precur-
sors 3 aa and Z/E-4 aa with diff erent ratios at 100 ° C
after 8.5 hours all led to the formation of 5 aa
exclusively (Eqs. 4–6, Scheme 3). As a comparison,
the transformation of allylicazide precursors 3 aa and
Z/E-4 aa with the palladium catalyst was accomplished
in only 3 hours, indicating that the palladium catalyst
may accelerate the the azide-alkyne cycloaddition
process (Eq. 7, Scheme 3).
[22]
Based on the experimental results, a rationale was
proposed in Scheme 4 by taking the reaction of 1 a as
an example. First, the oxidative addition of iodoben-
zene with Pd(0) formed arylpalladium Int-3, which
would undergo insertion with the allene unit to aff ord
(π-allyl)palladium intermediate Int-4. The (π-allyl)
palladium species Int-4 would accept nucleophilic
attack of azide anion to provide the three allylic azide
precursors 3 aa and Z/E-4 aa. Finally , the intramolecu-

Conclusion
W e have developed an efficient approach for the highly
selective construction of [4.3.0]-bicyclic 1,2,3-triazole
derivatives via a palladium-catalyzed three-component
tandem reaction of allenynes, or ganic iodides, and
NaN
3
. Owing to the importance of the bicyclic 1,2,3-
triazole structure as well as the good tolerance of
synthetically attractive functionalities such as meth-
oxyl, halogen, trifluoromethyl, ketone, and ester , this
method would be useful in or ganic synthesis and
medicinal chemistry . After careful mechanistic studies,
a mechanism involving the interconverting between
allylicazides is proposed. Further studies are being
pursued in this laboratory .
